title: Certificates of Deposit: When a Grace-Period Withdrawal Counts as the Owner's Own
content:
Not every penalized withdrawal made in grace from PCB Certificates of Deposit is credited back as a bank error. The bank first asks whether the withdrawal was the owner's own, judged by where its money went. This page states that test.

## Rule

A withdrawal made in grace counts as the owner's own if the money:

- was paid out by official check; or
- landed in one of the owner's own accounts at the bank, whether checking or savings.

Where the proceeds went is read from the withdrawal entry itself: its destination, and, where the destination is an account, the receiving account it names. Whether that receiving account belongs to the owner is read from the owner's own checking and savings accounts at the bank.

Where the money of a penalized withdrawal landed in someone else's account, not one of the owner's, the penalty is treated as a disputed transaction. It is not credited back under the rules for grace-period penalties.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical withdrawal entries)

| Destination on the withdrawal entry | Receiving account | Owner's own withdrawal? |
|---|---|---|
| Official check | none | Yes |
| Checking | the owner's own checking account | Yes |
| Savings | the owner's own savings account, since closed | Yes; it is the owner's account |
| Savings | a savings account held by a different customer | No; handled as a disputed transaction |
| Checking | an account reference found among none of the owner's accounts | No; handled as a disputed transaction |
